text: The appraisal and NPA asset product of rwb-source-data and the case-move answer of rwb-case are consumed on their documented shapes with a placeholder for the operation name, and are faked until their owners publish the names.
why: No source publishes the operation names and the C row of this slice is None, so the build cannot wait for them at wave 3.
read: Architecture v5 slide 8; Ownership Map; TSD S5 T5.2; legacy RWB-E4-022 Endpoints
applied_in: RWB-S5-E4022-APP s3 and s12.2; RWB-S5-E4022-CON s12.2 and s12.8
confirm: Owner of rwb-source-data (P1) and owner of rwb-case (P3) at the contract tag
impact: Two consumed rows and one fake carry the placeholder; a published name replaces it in a minor version.

text: The price of the current round is held against the round row of the listing with the ladder and its step as versioned reference data, and no column is added to rwb_asset for it.
why: R-DIS-38 conditions on price_at_round and TSD S5 T3.1 names no such column; inventing one would break the rule that no value a business person may change is written in code and no source value is invented.
read: TSD S5 T3.1 and T3.2; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-38
confirm: Solution architect and the DB story of the service at the physical schema review
impact: No migration is written for the round price; the value lives with the round and the gap stays open until the LDM names a column.

text: POST /assets/{assetId}/listings is declared once for the pricing story and the price step; the pricing story owns the start price and the head of NPA approval of the floor, and this slice owns the step of the price at each round and the reset of the inputs on an accepted re-appraisal.
why: Both stories list the operation and no source splits it, so an assumption is the only way to keep one declared surface and two builds.
read: TSD S5 T-A.1 and T-A.2; FSD S5 A2.11 and A2.13; legacy RWB-E4-022 Endpoints
applied_in: RWB-S5-E4022-APP s7 and s12.1; RWB-S5-E4022-CON s12.1
confirm: Solution architect of S5 and the pricing story owner at the contract tag
impact: One operation, one shape, two behaviours; the approval path of the floor is tested by the pricing story only.

text: The slice traces to FEAT-AST-13 of FSD S5 A2.13 and to BR-027 of the epic BRD while the PRD reference reads Pending (C1).
why: The split plan carries no requirement id for this slice and the header fixes the PRD reference text.
read: Story row of the slice with reqs []; FSD S5 T8; Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1
confirm: Business analyst when the PRD of S5 allocates requirement ids
impact: Traceability rows name the feature and the business requirement, not a requirement id.

text: The DISPOSAL package is loaded in force through the service template without an H row for RWB-PLT-E1072-CON or a C row for RWB-P7-E1073-CON in this slice, because DP-04 is outside the pattern set of the story rows.
why: The patterns of the slice are DP03, DP05, DP13 and DP19, which add only the decision-record and composite-route rows, and no source says which pattern carries the package load.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-04; story row patterns; FSD S5 A2.13.3.1; TSD S5 T4
applied_in: RWB-S5-E4022-APP s3 and s13; RWB-S5-E4022-CON s4 and s13
confirm: Solution architect at the pattern-set review of the service
impact: The dependency row of the story is unchanged; a later pattern revision may add the platform row.
